summary: The phylogeny side is ready (Open Tree opentree16.1, 2.39 M tips, open API) and chromosome number is tabulated for ~18,000 animal species (ACC) and for plants (CCDB API). The embryological side is not: no open table codes cleavage type (radial/bilateral/spiral) or yolk class across animal species; BioImage Archive has embryo images for a few model species only, and the one large egg dataset (6,700+ insect species, Dryad pv40d2r, CC0) covers egg size in a single class with uniform cleavage mode.
next_step: Compile a species-by-character matrix of cleavage type and yolk class from embryology texts/reviews (e.g., for ~200 representative metazoans), map to OTT ids, then pre-register a phylogenetic-signal test using the Open Tree induced subtree; chromosome number can be added from ACC.
obstacles_confirmed: No single open database comprehensively codes early embryological traits.
Cleavage mode and yolk class are not in a single open table and must be compiled.
Species sampling is concentrated in model organisms.
